recipes.name: Colcannon
ingredients_raw: 2 small leeks, cleaned and thinly sliced

steps.text: Place potatoes in a large pot and cover with salted water; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer until tender, about 15 to 20 minutes. Drain.
While potatoes are boiling, simmer or steam cabbage in a separate pot until tender. Drain and chop; set aside and keep warm.
Place leeks in a small pot; add just enough milk to cover. Simmer over low heat until leeks are soft, about 3 to 5 minutes.

Season potatoes with salt, pepper, and mace; mash well. Stir in cooked leeks and milk. Stir in cabbage and heat through until potatoes are pale green in color. Make a well in the center of the colcannon and pour in the melted butter. Mix well and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Colcannon
raw_recipe.description: These colcannon potatoes are a delicious blend of creamy mashed potatoes, tender leeks, green cabbage, and butter for a classic Irish side dish.

review.reviewBody: i didn't have mace on hand so i went out and bought it. on the back of the container it had a "flavorful tip" saying that 1/4 tsp ground mace = 1 tsp ground nutmeg. i had nutmeg at home and wouldn't have spent $4.50 on mace that i probably won't use again. oh well, now i know for next time. hope this helps somebody. happy cooking!

This is one of my all-time favorite comfort foods. The only addition I have made is to use half and half instead of milk for added richness.
This is wonderful with Roast chicken and I have done it for 200 guests at a fundraiser paired with roast pork loin.

I saw this recipe featured on St. Patty's Day and saved it. I just now made it and am sorry that I didn't make it earlier. I used kale instead of broccoli only because I had kale in the fridge and also wanted the dish to turn out greener in color. Yum! The flavors of the leeks, potatoes and kale together along with the little bit of ground mace was delicious. Just be careful on how much mace you put into this dish because it can overwhelm the other flavors. The recipe says a pinch and it means a pinch. I always tend to go heavier on herbs and spices, but not on mace because it's strong. The overall appearance is exactly as photographed and is a crowd pleaser. I really enjoyed Colcannon.

Yum! I made this for a potluck dinner party at my boss's house. It was a huge success. I used Yukon gold potatoes, which I cut in chunks, boiled and then cooled and peeled. The skins came right off with my fingers - much easier than peeling the raw potato. I think Yukons are best for mashed potatoes - not too waxy and not too dry. 

I sliced the cabbage and leeks into roughly 1/2 by 1 inch pieces, separating the layers as I put them in a dutch oven. Some people suggested sauteing the cabbage and leeks in butter, but I think that would have made the dish to greasy. Instead, I cooked the cabbage and the leeks together with enough Half & Half to cover over very, very low heat, so it wouldn't scorch and ruin the whole thing. This probably took an hour, stirring about every 10 min. I set the timer on the stove, and it just about coordinates with the frequency of commercials on TV! When they were tender, I poured off the H&H to use later and thoroughly drained the cabbage and leeks in a colander. Then I rough mashed everything together with a hand masher, adding the leftover H&H as needed. In this dish, I like the potatoes to be a little chunky, so they stand up to the cabbage and leeks.

As the finishing touch, I sprang for Irish butter (Kerrygold)- much creamier and authentic. I made this the night before and then warmed it up for a couple of hours and served from my crock pot. 

Finally, I am going to blend the left overs with some of the left over H&H to make a potato soup!
I prefer to saute the cabbage in butter to boiling it.

I saw this recipe featured on St. Patty's Day and saved it. I had planned to make it with Corned Beef Brisket as a side, but didn't get around to making this until later. I substituted nutmeg for the mace since I didn't want to drive to the market. I loved the taste of the dish but seemed a little unfinished/unmelded. So, I took the leftovers, put them in a baking dish, mixed in a 1/2 c. heavy cream, additional nutmeg and baked it off in the oven at 300 for 45 minutes. Oh! Over the top goodness. Yum! The flavors of the leeks, potatoes and cabbage together along with the little bit of ground nutmeg was delicious, perfect comfort food. I will make this again and experiment with kale or sub in Napa cabbage. I really enjoyed Colcannon.
I followed the recipe but used prepackaged shredded cabbage and left out the mace. Came out perfect, will definitely make again!
Sauted the vegies in oil/butter. Used yukon potatoes. The combo of the crunch of the vegetables and the creaminess of the potato was fabulous!

I made this and served it with our corned beef for family dinner. The adaptations mainly due to complications with timing were to cool down the sliced leeks, garlic, and cabbage in some butter and olive oil till lightly golden and then add to the smashed potatoes with additional butter and seasoning. I used a small about of nutmeg because of having no mace on hand. While the recipe was not strictly followed it was a huge inspiration and followed as much as possible. It was beautiful and delicious.

I love Colcannon and it's one of my favorite comfort foods. This was my first recipe for it many years ago. The only things I do differently (and to each their own)-I steam the cabbage vs. boiling it and use green onions instead of leeks. Heavy cream in lieu of the milk tends to make it fluffier and give a richer flavor. I agree with others that there's never too much butter for potatoes! Thank you for the recipe!

I stumbled onto Colcannon because I had leftover leeks, cabbage and kale from a soup I made, and needed something to do with them. I can't believe just how unbelievably good this was, even though I had very high hopes. I don't usually cook with butter, so maybe it was the 1/2 cup that did it :) I also used fresh ground nutmeg rather than mace. 

I sauteed half cabbage (2 cups) and half kale (2 cups) in the butter, and simmered the leeks (2 med. was about 4 cups of leeks chopped) in the milk. AMAZING!!!!! I'm pretty sure I used more than 1 lb. of potatoes though, and I'm so glad I did. I will be sorry when the last of it is gone! The tastiest "comfort" food in the world, and (other than the butter) very nutritious!

I like Colcannon. This recipe is very busy. I modified to use less pots, pans and dishes. I made it in a 15” Carbon Steel Paella pan - braised cabbage & combined all in the one pan. So; one-less pan - worked great. Served as a side to Broiled Rib Eye; paired well!

I use this as my base recipe. I saute the cabbage instead of boiling because not a fan of the texture of boiled cabbage. And I use a bunch of green onions instead of leeks. People love this as a base for beef stew or bangers. It is requested every year on St Patrick's day.

I have used this recipe MANY times.... love it! I also want to bring up the subject of people changing the recipe and then giving it any rating at all! Too many people used Kale and not cabbage, then proceed to give it fewer than the 5 stars it deserves! REVIEW THE RECIPE AS WRITTEN PEOPLE!

Loved it and made it again at Halloween last year. No changes to the recipe except for cutting the ingredients by half. Just enough cabbage, leeks, and mace to make mashed potato the hit of my dinner.

I decided to try this for our St. Patty's Day dinner. I used diced brussel sprouts instead of cabbage and a sweet onion instead of leeks. It needs more seasoning of some kind in addition to mace, which I had. It was a great addition to the corned beef. I also put some Dubliner cheddar on top when I served it. Yum!
I did not add the mace. Still delicious!

Mine doesn't look like the photo that comes with this recipe for I mashed it all pretty well. I actually had to adjust the quantity of milk higher because I had a bit more vegetables than the recipe calls for. But mashed well, it turned out to have awesome flavor, a definite comfort food.
Very delicious. My boys liked it too, and they don't like cabbage. I used 1/4 less butter and it turned out rich. I used onion and green onions because that is what I had at hand.
